project.name: dimos
project.description: Dimensional (DimOS) is a Python-based agentive operating system for generalist robotics, providing an SDK for navigation, perception, spatial memory, and natural-language control across humanoids, quadrupeds, drones, and robotic arms without requiring ROS. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.summary: Snapshot dataclass reporting engagement state, current poses, and button state for both hands.

nodes.name: QuestTeleopConfig
nodes.summary: Configuration for the Quest teleop module: control loop frequency and web server port.

nodes.name: QuestTeleopModule
nodes.summary: Main Quest teleop module: serves the browser teleop UI over a WebSocket, decodes Joy/PoseStamped frames, runs an engage/disengage state machine, and publishes processed pose and button streams at a fixed control rate.

nodes.name: quest_types.py
nodes.summary: Defines typed data containers for Quest controller state (axes, buttons, thumbstick) and a Buttons descriptor-style class with bitmask analog trigger packing.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses dynamic __getattr__/__setattr__ to expose named boolean flags backed by an integer bitfield, with reserved bits for packed analog trigger values.

nodes.name: ThumbstickState
nodes.summary: Lightweight dataclass holding the x/y axes of a thumbstick.

nodes.name: QuestControllerState
nodes.summary: Structured per-hand controller state decoded from a Joy message into named button flags, trigger values, and thumbstick axes.

nodes.name: Buttons
nodes.summary: Bitmask-backed button state with named flag accessors, analog trigger packing into reserved bits, and a factory to build from a pair of QuestControllerState instances.

nodes.name: path_utils.py
nodes.summary: Tiny utility exposing get_project_root() to resolve the repository root from any module location.

nodes.name: get_project_root
nodes.summary: Returns the dimos project root as a pathlib.Path by walking up from this file location.

nodes.name: robot_web_interface.py
nodes.summary: Thin wrapper exposing the RobotWebInterface class that subclasses a FastAPI/web server base for serving robot-facing HTTP and WebSocket routes.

nodes.name: RobotWebInterface
nodes.summary: Robot-side web interface class that wires up a configurable HTTP/WebSocket server used by teleop and visualization modules.

nodes.name: commons.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the PoseWithTime::setTime helper that converts integer sec/nsec ROS-style timestamps into a fractional seconds field used by the PGO pipeline.

nodes.name: commons.h
nodes.summary: Declares shared PGO data types PoseWithTime (translation + rotation + timestamp) and CloudWithPose (PCL point cloud bundled with a pose).
nodes.languageNotes: Header-only struct definitions using Eigen and PCL aliases.

nodes.name: dimos_native_module.hpp
nodes.summary: Base class for native C++ modules in the dimos nav stack: parses --key=value CLI args, provides typed accessors (string/float/int/bool), and emits ROS-compatible Header/timestamp helpers.
nodes.languageNotes: Header-only class with templated arg accessors and an atomic sequence counter for header IDs.

nodes.name: main.cpp
nodes.summary: Entry point for the pose-graph-optimization (PGO) native module: subscribes to odometry and registered scan topics, feeds them into SimplePGO, runs loop closure, and publishes corrected odometry and a fused global cloud.
nodes.languageNotes: Single-binary ROS-like node with concurrent producer (subscribers) and consumer (PGO loop) using mutex-guarded queues.

nodes.name: point_cloud_utils.hpp
nodes.summary: Conversion helpers between sensor_msgs/PointCloud2 (smartnav wire format) and pcl::PointCloud<PointXYZI>, plus a quaternion-to-RPY utility used throughout the PGO module.

nodes.name: simple_pgo.cpp
nodes.summary: Implementation of the SimplePGO class: keyframe selection, GTSAM ISAM2 factor-graph construction, ICP-based loop pair search, and incremental smoothing/update producing the global pose offset.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses GTSAM ISAM2 for incremental graph optimization and PCL ICP with KD-tree neighbour search for loop detection.

nodes.name: simple_pgo.h
nodes.summary: Public interface for SimplePGO: declares KeyPoseWithCloud, LoopPair, Config structs and the SimplePGO class that owns the keyframe set, factor graph, and current global offset.

nodes.name: PoseWithTime
nodes.summary: Bundle of a 3D translation, rotation matrix, and timestamp (sec/nsec plus combined seconds) representing a pose in time for SLAM messages.

nodes.name: CloudWithPose
nodes.summary: Pairs a PCL point cloud with a PoseWithTime so registered scans can be queued and processed atomically downstream.

nodes.name: NativeModule
nodes.summary: Base class that parses --key=value command-line arguments into a string map and exposes typed lookups (arg, arg_float, arg_int, arg_bool, has) for derived native modules.

nodes.name: make_header
nodes.summary: Builds a ROS-style Header struct with monotonically increasing seq, timestamp from seconds, and the supplied frame_id.

nodes.name: Handlers
nodes.summary: Topic-subscription callbacks that convert incoming odometry and registered point cloud messages into PoseWithTime/CloudWithPose entries and push them onto thread-safe queues.

nodes.name: on_odometry
nodes.summary: Subscriber callback that decodes an odometry message into rotation/translation/timestamp and enqueues it for the main PGO loop.

nodes.name: on_registered_scan
nodes.summary: Subscriber callback that converts an incoming PointCloud2 message into a CloudWithPose using the latest matching odometry pose and enqueues it.

nodes.name: build_odometry
nodes.summary: Assembles a ROS-style Odometry message from a rotation, translation, timestamp, and frame ids for publishing corrected poses downstream.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: PGO node entry: parses CLI args, wires subscribers and publishers, drives the optimization loop (key-pose insertion, loop search, smoothing) and publishes corrected odometry plus a downsampled global cloud.

nodes.name: build_pointcloud2
nodes.summary: Serializes a vector of XYZI points into a sensor_msgs/PointCloud2-compatible byte layout with field metadata for x/y/z/intensity.

nodes.name: parse_pointcloud2
nodes.summary: Deserializes a PointCloud2 byte buffer into a vector of PointXYZI by memcpy-ing the x/y/z/intensity fields out of each row.

nodes.name: quat_to_rpy
nodes.summary: Converts a unit quaternion (qx, qy, qz, qw) into roll/pitch/yaw Euler angles with singularity handling near the poles.

nodes.name: KeyPoseWithCloud
nodes.summary: Keyframe record holding the local and global rotation/translation, timestamp, and body-frame point cloud retained for loop closure.

nodes.name: LoopPair
nodes.summary: Describes a detected loop closure: source/target keyframe indices, the relative rotation/translation offset, and the ICP fitness score.

nodes.name: Config
nodes.summary: Tunable thresholds for the PGO pipeline: keyframe spacing, loop search radius, fitness/time/score gates, submap range and resolution, and minimum loop detection duration.

nodes.name: SimplePGO
nodes.summary: Stateful pose-graph-optimizer: owns the keyframe set, GTSAM ISAM2 graph, ICP instance, and exposes APIs to add key poses, detect loops, smooth and update, and read the current global offset.

nodes.name: SimplePGO
nodes.summary: Constructor that stores the Config, allocates the GTSAM ISAM2 solver, resets the global offset, and configures the PCL ICP aligner (iterations, distance, epsilons, RANSAC).

nodes.name: isKeyPose
nodes.summary: Returns true when the input pose is far enough in translation or rotation from the previous keyframe to be promoted into the graph.

nodes.name: addKeyPose
nodes.summary: Adds a new keyframe to the GTSAM factor graph: anchors the first pose with a PriorFactor and adds BetweenFactors derived from the local-frame delta to the previous keyframe.

nodes.name: getSubMap
nodes.summary: Builds a downsampled local submap by transforming a window of keyframe clouds into a common frame and applying a voxel-grid filter at the configured resolution.

nodes.name: searchForLoopPairs
nodes.summary: Detects loop closures by KD-tree neighbour search on keyframe positions followed by ICP alignment of source/target submaps, recording successful pairs with their relative transforms and fitness scores.

nodes.name: smoothAndUpdate
nodes.summary: Adds cached loop-pair BetweenFactors to the graph, runs several ISAM2 update iterations, writes the optimized global poses back to each keyframe, and recomputes the cumulative global offset.

nodes.name: cloud_filter.hpp
nodes.summary: Header-only PCL-based point cloud filtering utility providing voxel-grid downsampling and statistical outlier removal for LiDAR pre-processing in the FAST-LIO2 pipeline.
nodes.languageNotes: Header-only C++ template using PCL VoxelGrid and StatisticalOutlierRemoval filters; instantiated for arbitrary PointT types.

nodes.name: main.cpp
nodes.summary: Entry point for the FAST-LIO2 + Livox Mid-360 native module that bridges the Livox SDK2 to FAST-LIO-NON-ROS, performing EKF-LOAM SLAM and publishing registered point clouds and odometry via LCM.
nodes.languageNotes: C++17 with multithreaded SDK callbacks, atomic flags for shutdown, and LCM messaging; integrates a header-only FAST-LIO core with a global VoxelMap for free-space management.

nodes.name: voxel_map.hpp
nodes.summary: Header-only global voxel map with hash-based O(1) insert/update, distance pruning, and raycasting-based free-space clearing using Amanatides & Woo 3D DDA over a dynamically discovered sensor FOV.
nodes.languageNotes: Custom spatial hash with large-prime mixing; templated insert/raycast methods accept any PCL PointT; FOV is discovered from elevation angles in sensor-local frame using quaternion conjugate rotation.

nodes.name: quat_rotate
nodes.summary: Rotates a 3D vector by a unit quaternion using the v + 2*cross(q.xyz, cross(q.xyz, v) + q.w*v) form, used to apply the configured initial pose orientation offset.

nodes.name: publish_lidar
nodes.summary: Serializes a PCL point cloud into a sensor_msgs.PointCloud2 LCM message, applying the initial-pose offset to each point and publishing on the configured LiDAR topic.

nodes.name: publish_odometry
nodes.summary: Composes a nav_msgs.Odometry LCM message from FAST-LIO pose output, applying the user-configured initial pose offset to both position and orientation via quaternion multiplication.

nodes.name: on_point_cloud
nodes.summary: Livox SDK callback that converts raw cartesian-high or cartesian-low LiDAR points into a Livox CustomMsg buffered for the main SLAM processing loop.

nodes.name: on_imu_data
nodes.summary: Livox SDK callback that converts raw IMU samples into a custom_messages::Imu message and feeds it directly into the FastLio state estimator.

nodes.name: on_info_change
nodes.summary: Livox SDK callback fired on device connect that switches the lidar into normal work mode and enables IMU data streaming.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Program entry point that parses CLI arguments, initialises the Livox SDK and FAST-LIO state, then runs the main SLAM loop: drains buffered point clouds, runs SLAM, raycasts and prunes the voxel map, and publishes lidar/odometry/map outputs at the configured frequency.

nodes.name: simulator_base.py
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract SimulatorBase class establishing a unified interface (init, get_stage, close) for backend-specific simulators like Isaac and Genesis.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Python ABC with @abstractmethod to enforce the simulator contract.

nodes.name: SimulatorBase
nodes.summary: Abstract base class that defines the common simulator contract with abstract methods for initialization, retrieving the active stage/scene, and shutdown.

nodes.name: simulator.py
nodes.summary: Genesis simulator implementation that configures a viewer scene and loads heterogeneous entity types (mesh, URDF, MJCF, primitives) declared via dict configs.
nodes.languageNotes: Bridges Dimos' abstract simulator API to the genesis library's morph/scene primitives.

nodes.name: GenesisSimulator
nodes.summary: Concrete Genesis-backed simulator that builds a configured Scene with viewer/visualization options and dispatches entity-config dicts to the appropriate gs.morphs constructors.

nodes.name: simulator.py
nodes.summary: Isaac Sim simulator implementation that boots a SimulationApp with optional USD loading and exposes the active USD stage through the SimulatorBase interface.
nodes.languageNotes: Lazy-imports omni.usd inside get_stage to avoid pulling Omniverse modules at import time.

nodes.name: IsaacSimulator
nodes.summary: Concrete Isaac Sim simulator wrapper that initializes the headless/USD-aware SimulationApp and provides access to the current USD stage.

nodes.name: stream_base.py
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract base class StreamBase for simulator video streaming, declaring the common lifecycle (load stage, set up camera, ffmpeg, annotator, stream, cleanup) and shared ffmpeg pipe setup used by concrete simulator implementations.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Python ABC with @abstractmethod to enforce a template-method pattern across concrete simulator stream backends.

nodes.name: StreamBase
nodes.summary: Abstract base class establishing the streaming pipeline (USD stage loading, camera setup, ffmpeg subprocess, annotator) and concrete _setup_ffmpeg implementation shared by Genesis and Isaac stream backends.

nodes.name: stream.py
nodes.summary: Concrete StreamBase implementation for the Genesis simulator: builds the scene, attaches a camera, renders frames per step, and pipes RGB output through ffmpeg.

nodes.name: GenesisStream
nodes.summary: Genesis-specific stream that builds the scene, attaches a camera, steps the simulation, and streams rendered frames to ffmpeg while logging step/render/transmit timing.

nodes.name: stream.py
nodes.summary: Concrete StreamBase implementation for NVIDIA Isaac Sim: opens a USD stage, attaches an annotator-backed render product, and streams orchestrated frames to ffmpeg.

nodes.name: IsaacStream
nodes.summary: Isaac Sim stream that loads a USD stage, creates a render product against a camera prim, attaches an annotator, and pipes orchestrated frames to ffmpeg with per-stage timing diagnostics.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: CUDA 12.8 GPU container that packages NVIDIA's GraspGen grasp-pose generation model with PyTorch 2.7, custom CUDA extensions (pointnet2_ops, torch-scatter, torch-cluster), and pre-extracted Robotiq 2F-140 checkpoints for runtime grasp inference.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Miniconda inside the CUDA devel base image to isolate a Python 3.10 'app' environment; sets TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST for multi-GPU architecture compilation (Ampere through Hopper plus 12.0) and forces CUDA builds for pointnet2_ops extensions.

nodes.name: cuda
nodes.summary: Single-stage build derived from nvidia/cuda:12.8.1-cudnn-devel-ubuntu22.04 that installs GraspGen and its model checkpoints into /app/GraspGen with environment defaults pointing at the robotiq_2f_140 gripper.

nodes.name: _docker-build-template.yml
nodes.summary: Reusable workflow_call template that builds and pushes a Docker image to ghcr.io with aggressive disk-space cleanup, branch-based image pruning, and GitHub Actions cache for Docker layers.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses tiered cleanup heuristics (>60% triggers per-tag deduplication, >85% triggers aggressive purge keeping only main/dev tags) to manage self-hosted runner disk space.

nodes.name: autofix.yml
nodes.summary: Lightweight pull request workflow that runs ruff fix, ruff format, and uv lock, then uses autofix-ci to push the resulting changes back to the PR branch.

nodes.name: backport.yml
nodes.summary: Opens a backport PR onto release/* branches when a merged PR carries a 'backport release/<x>' label, leveraging korthout/backport-action.

nodes.name: ci.yml
nodes.summary: Primary CI workflow running mypy/pre-commit lint, Rust fmt/clippy/test across discovered Cargo crates, doc code-block execution, docs validation, a Python test matrix (3.10-3.14 plus free-threaded 3.14t), and self-hosted ROS tests, with a cross-job fail-fast watcher and an alls-green branch-protection gate.
nodes.languageNotes: Demonstrates a 'ci-complete' alls-green pattern for branch protection and a separate fail-fast watcher job to cancel sibling jobs the moment the matrix tests fail.

nodes.name: docker-build.yml
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the layered Docker image graph (ros, python, ros-python, dev, ros-dev, navigation) on push to main and weekly cron, using dorny/paths-filter to detect which Dockerfile dirs changed and chaining the reusable build template with branch-derived tags.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements a force-rebuild override for schedule/workflow_dispatch and a downstream image-dependency DAG where each child image inherits the parent's freshly-built tag (falling back to :latest).

nodes.name: release.yml
nodes.summary: Manually-dispatched release pipeline that validates the version against PyPI, builds sdist and cibuildwheel wheels for four OS/arch targets with SLSA build-provenance attestations, publishes to TestPyPI then PyPI via OIDC trusted publishing, creates a GPG-signed tag and GitHub Release, and opens a merge-back PR to main.
nodes.languageNotes: Filename is bound by PyPI's trusted publisher configuration and must not be renamed. Uses `-s ours` merge-back to preserve two-parent topology without dragging release-only commits into main.

nodes.name: stale.yml
nodes.summary: Daily cron workflow using actions/stale to mark PRs without recent activity as stale after 23 days and close them 7 days later, exempting 'pinned' and 'do-not-close' labels.

nodes.name: .codecov.yml
nodes.summary: Codecov configuration that disables PR comments and flag coverage carryforward to prevent noisy coverage reports on the dimos repository.

nodes.name: .dockerignore
nodes.summary: Docker build context exclusion rules that keep build artifacts, virtualenvs, datasets, model checkpoints, and node_modules out of container images for faster, leaner builds.

nodes.name: .pre-commit-config.yaml
nodes.summary: Pre-commit hook configuration wiring up ruff lint/format, mypy type checks, large-file guards, and other repo-wide quality gates that run on every commit.

nodes.name: AGENTS.md

nodes.name: CLA.md
nodes.summary: Individual Contributor License Agreement that contributors must sign before having pull requests merged into the Dimensional OS project.

nodes.name: README.md

nodes.name: avia.yaml
nodes.summary: FAST-LIO2 SLAM/odometry configuration tuned for the Livox Avia LiDAR: 6 scan lines, 90 degree FOV, 450 m range, with IMU extrinsics calibrated for the Avia housing and PCD saving enabled.
nodes.languageNotes: lidar_type=1 selects the Livox preprocessing path inside FAST-LIO2.

nodes.name: default.yaml
nodes.summary: Default FAST-LIO2 configuration used when no per-sensor preset is selected: 4 scan lines, 360 degree FOV, tightened IMU covariances and live extrinsic calibration enabled for an unspecified Livox device.
nodes.languageNotes: Smaller acc_cov/gyr_cov (0.01) than mid360 indicates tighter trust in the IMU and reduced det_range (60 m) for cleaner mapping.

nodes.name: horizon.yaml
nodes.summary: FAST-LIO2 SLAM configuration for the Livox Horizon LiDAR: 6 scan lines, 100 degree FOV, 260 m detection range with online IMU-LiDAR extrinsic estimation enabled.
nodes.languageNotes: extrinsic_est_en=true asks FAST-LIO2 to refine the IMU-to-LiDAR transform online during odometry.

nodes.name: marsim.yaml
nodes.summary: FAST-LIO2 configuration for the MARSim simulator (quadrotor sensor topics) using lidar_type 4, 90 degree FOV and a short 50 m detection range for simulated flight tests.
nodes.languageNotes: lidar_type=4 is a non-standard preprocessing branch added for MARSim's rendered point clouds.

nodes.name: mid360.yaml
nodes.summary: FAST-LIO2 SLAM configuration for the Livox Mid-360 LiDAR: 4 scan lines, full 360 degree FOV, 100 m range, with extrinsics matching the Mid-360 IMU offset on its mounting bracket.

nodes.name: ouster64.yaml
nodes.summary: FAST-LIO2 configuration for the 64-beam Ouster LiDAR: lidar_type 3, 180 degree FOV, 150 m range and nanosecond timestamps consumed from the os_cloud_node topics.
nodes.languageNotes: timestamp_unit=3 declares per-point timestamps are nanoseconds, required for Ouster's PointCloud2 format.

nodes.name: velodyne.yaml
nodes.summary: FAST-LIO2 configuration for a 32-beam Velodyne LiDAR at 10 Hz with microsecond timestamps, 180 degree FOV and 100 m range using the /velodyne_points and /imu/data topics.
nodes.languageNotes: scan_rate and timestamp_unit are Velodyne-specific preprocessing parameters not present in Livox configs.

nodes.name: architecture.md
nodes.summary: Architectural overview of the memory2 observation storage and streaming layer, describing the Store/Stream/Backend composition and supporting subsystems (BlobStore, Codecs, Transformers, Backpressure Buffers).
nodes.languageNotes: Includes ASCII pipeline diagram and a module/subpackage table mapping modules to their source files.

nodes.name: embeddings.md
nodes.summary: Design document for the memory2 embedding system, covering enrichment-not-replacement philosophy, observation types, the EmbedTransformer, vector search, multi-modal embeddings, chaining as cheap pre-filter, and how FTS is a separate concern.

nodes.name: intro.md
nodes.summary: Getting-started guide for the memory2 subsystem walking through quick start, filters, terminals, transforms, live queries, spatial + live patterns, and embeddings usage.

nodes.summary: Brief scratchpad of developer notes for the memory2 subsystem.

nodes.name: streaming.md

layers.name: Application & Robotics
layers.description: Robot-specific drivers and orchestration (Unitree, drones, alfred), high-level porcelain SDK, agent skills, web/FastAPI UI, and protocol-conformance specs that compose the rest of the system into runnable robotic platforms.

layers.name: Agentive Runtime
layers.description: LLM agent runtimes, MCP integration, planning loops, tool/skill dispatch, demos and harnesses that drive robots through natural-language control.

layers.name: Perception & World Modeling
layers.description: Detection, tracking, fiducials and spatial memory; mapping (OSM, Google Maps, occupancy); embedding/timeseries memory stores; segmentation and vision-language models; simulation engines and Rerun visualization bridges.

layers.name: Navigation, Manipulation & Control
layers.description: Planners, replanners, visual servoing and the nav_stack (FAST-LIO2, PGO, terrain); grasping, kinematics and motion tasks; control coordinator and adapters that produce actionable trajectories for robots.

layers.name: Hardware & I/O
layers.description: Sensor drivers (camera, lidar), drive-train and hardware adapters, audio/video streams (TTS, STT, providers) and teleoperation surfaces (Quest VR, joystick) that move data in and out of the system.

layers.name: Core Runtime & Protocol
layers.description: The Module/transport/RPC system, coordination daemon, blueprints and registries, pub/sub and TF protocol backends (LCM, Redis, ROS, SHM), RxPy backpressure strategies and shared exceptions that everything else builds on.

layers.name: Messages & Shared Types
layers.description: ROS-style message schemas (geometry, sensor, nav, std, vision, trajectory, tf2) plus shared type hints, vectors, robot capabilities/locations and constants used across every subsystem.

layers.name: Utilities & Tooling
layers.description: Cross-cutting helpers: logging, threadpools, transform utilities, LLM helpers and CLI tools (map, apriltag, calibrate), plus project policies and shared configuration utilities.

layers.name: Infrastructure & DevOps
layers.description: Containerization (Dockerfiles, dockerignore), Nix flakes and direnv shells, GitHub Actions workflows and reusable actions, pre-commit/codecov/pyproject build configs and packaging setup that defines how the project is built, tested and deployed.

layers.name: Documentation
layers.description: Top-level project documentation: README, AGENTS guide and CLA that orient new contributors and downstream users to the dimos platform.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to learn what DimOS is: a Python-first, ROS-free operating system for generalist robotics that runs on humanoids, quadrupeds, drones, and arms. The landing page sets expectations for the SDK's four pillars (navigation, perception, agentive control, spatial memory) and points to the install paths, supported hardware, and featured runfiles. Pair it with AGENTS.md, which is the contributor cheat-sheet: it enumerates blueprints, the @skill decorator, MCP tooling, and the repo layout you will see throughout this tour.

tour.title: Package Entry & Porcelain API
tour.description: Open dimos/__init__.py, the top-level package. It uses a module-level __getattr__ to lazily expose the Dimos porcelain class, so `import dimos` is cheap and only pulls in heavy submodules on first attribute access. That porcelain class lives in dimos/porcelain/dimos.py and is the user-facing surface for the whole SDK: it spawns a ModuleCoordinator under the hood, starts and stops blueprints, lists skills, peeks at live streams, and lets you connect to a running daemon — the single object that lets you ‘vibecode’ a robot in a few lines of Python.
tour.languageLesson: Python's module-level __getattr__ (PEP 562) turns a package into a lazy barrel: top-level names are resolved only when first accessed, letting heavy submodules (torch, ROS bindings, hardware drivers) stay un-imported until they are actually needed.

tour.title: The Module Abstraction
tour.description: Everything in DimOS is a Module. dimos/core/module.py is the most-imported file in the codebase (fan-in 120) and defines Module/ModuleBase, the foundational unit that wires inputs, outputs, RPCs, skills, tools, and transports into a self-describing reactive component with an async main lifecycle. dimos/core/core.py provides the @rpc decorator that marks a method as remote-callable across modules, which is the second half of the contract — together they make a module ‘a thing that publishes streams and answers RPC calls.’
tour.languageLesson: Python decorators like @rpc mutate a method's metadata at class-definition time, attaching markers that a metaclass or registry later scans. This is the same pattern Pydantic, FastAPI, and Django use to turn ordinary classes into self-describing components without boilerplate.

tour.title: Streams, Transports & RPC
tour.description: Modules don't call each other directly — they publish to typed streams and call each other over RPC. dimos/core/stream.py defines the Stream/In/Out/RemoteIn/RemoteOut primitives that form DimOS's publish/subscribe substrate. dimos/core/transport.py supplies the pluggable transport stack: LCM, shared memory, ROS, and Zenoh variants (with JPEG specialisations) so the same module can broadcast over whichever transport the deployment needs. dimos/protocol/pubsub/spec.py is the abstract interface family every transport implements, and dimos/protocol/rpc/rpc_utils.py round-trips Python exceptions across the wire so remote failures surface as real RemoteError objects on the caller.

tour.title: Blueprints & Coordination
tour.description: If Modules are the atoms, Blueprints are the molecules. dimos/core/coordination/blueprints.py defines Blueprint and BlueprintAtom plus stream/module reference types, giving you a declarative DSL for wiring module graphs (and an autoconnect helper that infers obvious links). dimos/core/coordination/module_coordinator.py is the central orchestrator that loads a blueprint, validates module references, applies stream remappings, and deploys each module onto a Python worker or a Docker worker. This is the runtime engine that Step 2's porcelain spins up for you.

tour.title: Agents, Skills & MCP
tour.description: DimOS is ‘agent-native’: LLMs drive the robot by calling skills. dimos/agents/annotation.py supplies the @skill decorator that stamps telemetry, times calls, and propagates skill context via ContextVar. dimos/agents/mcp/mcp_server.py is the FastAPI-based MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that exposes skill RPCs over JSON-RPC and SSE, while dimos/agents/mcp/mcp_client.py wraps an LLM with a LangChain agent loop that discovers those skills as tools and feeds tool-stream notifications back into the conversation. The README in dimos/agents/mcp/ explains how to drive this with the MCP Inspector. This is what makes ‘hey Robot, go find the kitchen’ work.
tour.languageLesson: ContextVar (from `contextvars`) gives async code thread-/task-local state that propagates correctly across `await` points — DimOS uses it so a deeply nested skill call can still read which skill invocation it belongs to without passing the context through every signature.

tour.title: Perception & Spatial Memory
tour.description: Perception is where the agent gets its eyes. dimos/perception/detection/module3D.py lifts 2D detections to 3D by intersecting bounding boxes with a lidar pointcloud and publishes Detection3DArray plus pose/quaternion data. dimos/perception/object_tracker.py combines OpenCV CSRT tracking with ORB-based re-identification, depth-aware Detection3D generation, and TF publication, producing the persistent ‘this is the same chair I saw before’ identity. dimos/perception/experimental/temporal_memory/temporal_memory.py wires image frames through a window accumulator, a VLM analyzer, and an entity graph DB to build the spatio-temporal RAG layer the agent queries with natural language.

tour.title: Manipulation: Pick-and-Place for Arms
tour.description: Manipulation is one of the most important capabilities for arms like the xArm + AgileX Piper. dimos/manipulation/manipulation_module.py is the core ManipulationModule that orchestrates motion planning, collision-aware path generation, trajectory dispatch, and multi-robot state management — it has fan-out 22, second-highest in the codebase, because it touches nearly every other subsystem. dimos/manipulation/pick_and_place_module.py builds on it to combine 3D detections from Step 7 with grasp generation and obstacle bookkeeping, so the agent can pick a named object and place it at a target pose. dimos/manipulation/blueprints.py wires camera + simulator + perception + MCP + manipulation into runnable end-to-end pick-and-place setups you can launch in one line.

tour.title: Navigation & the Control Coordinator
tour.description: For mobile robots, dimos/navigation/nav_stack/main.py is the top-level builder that wires planners, terrain analysis, PGO (pose graph optimization), and rerun visualization into one navigation blueprint. dimos/agents/skills/navigation.py exposes that stack to LLMs as agent skills: tag a location, navigate to a text/object/semantic query, or stop. For arms, the Control Coordinator README in dimos/control/ documents the tick loop, priority arbitration, preemption, and configuration model that lets multiple control tasks (servoing, IK, teleop) share the same hardware safely.

tour.title: Concrete Robot Drivers (Unitree)
tour.description: All the abstractions above only matter once they drive real hardware. dimos/robot/unitree/connection.py is the WebRTC connection that subscribes to LiDAR, video, and lowstate streams and publishes movement commands to Go2/G1 robots. dimos/robot/unitree/go2/connection.py specializes that for the Go2 quadruped, exposing motion-control RPCs and a ReplayConnection that re-streams recorded data for offline development. dimos/robot/unitree/go2/blueprints/smart/unitree_go2.py is the headline ‘smart Go2’ blueprint: it autoconnects the basic robot with voxel mapping, costmap, A* planner, frontier exploration, patrolling, and the movement manager — a complete autonomous quadruped from one Blueprint object.

tour.title: Quest VR Teleoperation
tour.description: Teleoperation is how humans ride the robot — and DimOS supports a Quest 3 VR headset as a first-class input. dimos/teleop/quest/quest_teleop_module.py is the core teleop module: it stands up a WebSocket server that browser-side WebXR code streams controller poses to, runs an engage/disengage control loop, and publishes Pose and button streams downstream. dimos/teleop/quest/blueprints.py wires that module to twist/arm teleop extensions, transports, and visualization, while dimos/control/blueprints/teleop.py drops the Quest input into a ControlCoordinator that runs Cartesian IK on the robot's arm. The teleop README explains the full pose/twist message flow from headset to motors.
tour.languageLesson: WebXR exposes 6-DoF controller poses to a browser via the immersive-vr session API. Streaming those poses over a WebSocket to a Python server (rather than running robotics code in the browser) keeps the hot loop in native land while letting any WebXR-capable headset act as the input device.

tour.title: Web Interface, Containerization & CI
tour.description: Closing the loop: dimos/web/fastapi_server.py is the FastAPI server that streams MJPEG video feeds and SSE text streams from DimOS observables to a browser, and dimos/web/robot_web_interface.py wraps it as RobotWebInterface for robot-facing HTTP and WebSocket routes — the same surface the Quest teleop UI from Step 11 mounts on. docker/python/Dockerfile is the curated Python+uv base image that the dev image layers on top of, and .github/workflows/docker-build.yml orchestrates the full layered image graph (ros, python, ros-python, dev, ros-dev, navigation) on push and weekly cron. pyproject.toml declares the dimos package, its per-robot/per-sensor optional dependency groups, console scripts, and uv sources — the single source of truth that ties every previous step together into a shippable package.
tour.languageLesson: pyproject.toml's `[project.optional-dependencies]` table (PEP 621) lets one package ship many install profiles — e.g. `pip install dimos[unitree-go2]` versus `dimos[xarm]` — so robotics users only download the heavy hardware SDKs they actually need.
